title: The Padres Cost $3.9 Billion. Winning Will Cost More.
secondaryKeywords: how padres can win world series
audience: A prospective owner, operator or investor who wants a sendable buyer's memo on how San Diego converts capital and players into a first World Series—written as a business feature, not a hot-take recap.
metaDescription: A buyer’s memo on baseball’s record franchise sale: what San Diego’s assets are worth, where the balance sheet breaks, and how to buy a title.
angle: Treat the record sale as an operating problem. Price the demand-side assets, name the two structural liabilities (empty pipeline, collapsed local media), locate the surplus contracts, then rank the six moves in the order a new owner should make them.

distribution.linkedinHook: A $3.9bn baseball club with the worst farm system in the sport, $858M owed to five players and no regional TV network. Here is the asset sheet.
distribution.shortFact: King and Miller cost $21M this season and have produced 5.6 wins. The five players owed $858M after 2026 have produced 4.5.
